PAID PARENTAL LEAVE SCHEME
1. Adoption: covered with the same entitlements when the child is under 5 years old at placement.
2. Secondary carer: 6 weeks of paid leave at full pay.
3. Primary carer: 22 weeks of paid leave; the first 12 weeks at full pay, the rest at 75% of pay. A multiple birth adds 6 weeks per additional child, paid at 75%.
4. Qualifying service: at least 6 full months of employment on the date of the birth or placement.
5. Notice: the request must be submitted at least 10 weeks before the first day of leave.
6. Timing: leave is one continuous block. It starts no earlier than the birth or placement date (a primary carer expecting a birth may start up to 6 weeks before the expected date) and no later than 12 months after that date. A request for more weeks than the entitlement cannot be approved as submitted.
7. Coverage: permanent and fixed-term employees with at least 16 contracted hours per week. Contractors and agency workers are not covered.

1. Coverage: permanent and fixed-term employees with at least 12 contracted hours per week. Contractors and agency workers are not covered.
2. Secondary carer: 4 weeks of paid leave at full pay.
3. Adoption: covered with the same entitlements when the child is under 12 years old at placement.
4. Primary carer: 20 weeks of paid leave; the first 14 weeks at full pay, the rest at 80% of pay. A multiple birth adds 6 weeks per additional child, paid at 80%.
5. Timing: leave is one continuous block. It starts no earlier than the birth or placement date (a primary carer expecting a birth may start up to 6 weeks before the expected date) and no later than 3 months after that date. A request for more weeks than the entitlement cannot be approved as submitted.
6. Qualifying service: at least 9 full months of employment on the date of the birth or placement.
7. Notice: the request must be submitted at least 8 weeks before the first day of leave.

2. Qualifying service: at least 6 full months of employment on the date of the birth or placement.
3. Timing: leave is one continuous block. It starts no earlier than the birth or placement date (a primary carer expecting a birth may start up to 4 weeks before the expected date) and no later than 12 months after that date. A request for more weeks than the entitlement cannot be approved as submitted.
4. Primary carer: 26 weeks of paid leave; the first 15 weeks at full pay, the rest at 80% of pay. A multiple birth adds 4 weeks per additional child, paid at 80%.
5. Secondary carer: 2 weeks of paid leave at full pay.
6. Notice: the request must be submitted at least 4 weeks before the first day of leave.
7. Coverage: permanent and fixed-term employees and contractors with at least 24 contracted hours per week. Agency workers are not covered.

2. Timing: leave is one continuous block. It starts no earlier than the birth or placement date (a primary carer expecting a birth may start up to 11 weeks before the expected date) and no later than 6 months after that date. A request for more weeks than the entitlement cannot be approved as submitted.
3. Secondary carer: 2 weeks of paid leave at full pay.
4. Adoption: covered with the same entitlements when the child is under 18 years old at placement.
5. Primary carer: 12 weeks of paid leave; the first 7 weeks at full pay, the rest at 75% of pay. A multiple birth adds 2 weeks per additional child, paid at 75%.
6. Notice: the request must be submitted at least 12 weeks before the first day of leave.
7. Qualifying service: at least 6 full months of employment on the date of the birth or placement.
